question_text: Were all modified loan eligibility requirements met?

applicability.source_sql: SELECT DISTINCT Loans.LoanID FROM Loans  WHERE (Loans.QC_Policy = 'Fannie Mae')

defect_options.response: Mtg Modification changed the loan terms of original Note

finding.description: The mortgage modification in place changed the original terms from the original Note and is not permittable by FNMA.

notes: Single substantive defect option (O-FNM-50226) captures the blanket 'modification changed original note terms' outcome. B2-1.5-02's Modified Loans subsection carves out several eligible-modification categories (converted ARMs, principal curtailment/recast, construction-to-perm, NY consolidation) not separately distinguished by this ACES option -- noted for atomic-rule nuance, not a card-level compile blocker.

question_text: Were all nonstandard payment collection options eligibility requirements met?

applicability.source_sql: SELECT DISTINCT Loans.LoanID FROM Loans  WHERE (Loans.QC_Policy = 'Fannie Mae')

defect_options.response: A non-monthly payment option offered without a separate agreement

finding.description: The subject loan is ineligible for delivery due to an unacceptable non-standard payment option.

notes: Single substantive option covers the 'terms embedded in loan docs without a separate agreement' failure mode. The guide's 3-part conditions for an acceptable separate-agreement nonstandard-payment plan (no impact to note terms/reporting, cancelable without cost, lender-identifiable) are not separately enumerated as their own exception codes.

notes: Single exception code (O-FNM-00713) representing one holistic judgment verdict; matches docs/taxonomy.md's scripted_review example directly ('layered-risk adequacy'). The guide section's many risk factors are handled as a multi-item criteria checklist within one atomic rule rather than as separate bundled exception codes, so no bundle decomposition is needed.

compile.nuance: 4 of 13 defect options carry generic (non O-FNM-prefixed) ACES codes -- Title 90Days, TitleRedFlags, Title-TitleReqmts, Title-TransofTitle -- with no dedicated Selling Guide provision located in this corpus (e.g. no explicit 90-day/180-day title-commitment-effective-date rule was found in B7-2-05 or elsewhere). They sit within the general title-exceptions scope of B7-2-05 but their specific parameters (day-count window, 'red flag' criteria, chain-of-title narrative) read as lender/ACES-standard overlays layered on top of, rather than directly cited from, FNMA Selling Guide text.

notes: 13 substantive defect options span attorney-title-opinion-letter mechanics (6 options, fully grounded in B7-2-06), title insurer approval (B7-2-02), title exceptions/impediments/red-flags/chain-of-title (B7-2-05), and general title insurance provision/coverage (B7-2-01, O-FNM-00830). See compile.nuance for the 4 options without precise dedicated grounding.
